title: Unified Inference — Product PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (v27)
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Comprehensive PRD for Unified Inference v27: goals, requirements, high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing/packaging updates, and release notes for the June 2026 release.
body:
Overview:

This document describes the product requirements, design, roadmap, pricing changes, and release notes for Unified Inference v27 (June 2026). Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's core product that provides a single API and operational model for running LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. v27 focuses on three themes: predictable performance for multi-tenant workloads, streamlined pricing/packaging for mid-market customers, and expanded rollout controls for enterprise customers.

Goals and Success Metrics:

- Primary goals:
  - Reduce 95th-percentile tail latency for multi-tenant Hosted endpoints by 20% under baseline traffic patterns.
  - Introduce a new "Reserved Plus" pricing tier targeted at mid-market customers to improve conversion from self-serve trials by 15%.
  - Ship canary-aware rollouts and route-level circuit breakers for enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Success metrics (90-day post-launch):
  - 95th P50/P95 latency improvement: P95 <= baseline * 0.80 for multi-tenant routes.
  - Pricing conversion: trial -> paid conversion rate for mid-market up 15% quarter-over-quarter.
  - Reliability: rollout-related incidents <= 1 per quarter; automatic fallback engaged in >= 90% of simulated failovers.

Target personas:

- Product/Platform Engineers integrating Redwood API into product features.
- ML Engineers optimizing model choices and quantization for cost/latency.
- Platform/Infra teams purchasing Dedicated/Private capacity at mid-market and enterprise.

Key Features (v27):

1) Multi-tenant performance isolation improvements
- Dynamic request shaping per-customer token quota to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Prefix-aware KV cache partitioning to reduce cross-tenant cache pollution.
- Adaptive batching thresholds based on incoming request variance.

2) Canary-aware rollouts and route-level circuit breakers
- Canary flagging per-route with automatic monitoring of quality regressions and latency SLOs.
- Route circuit breakers with configurable thresholds (error rate, latency, token cost) and automated fallback to compatible model variants.

3) Pricing & Packaging: Reserved Plus
- New Reserved Plus tier (monthly commit) combining predictable capacity with limited burst credits and a simplified unit price for embeddings and text tokens.
- Self-serve upgrade path from free/usage plan to Reserved Plus in the Console.

4) Observability & Cost Controls
- Token-level cost breakdown per-route and per-model in Console.
- New optimization suggestions panel (batching, cache, quantization) surfaced in product pages.

Functional Requirements:

- FR-001: API-level canary flag that accepts: route_id, canary_percentage, model_variant, metric_thresholds, and rollback_policy.
- FR-002: Circuit breaker configuration per-route supporting thresholds for latency (ms), error_rate (%), and token_cost ($).
- FR-003: Pricing engine must support Reserved Plus commitments with monthly billing and burst credits accounting.
- FR-004: Console UI to surface cost suggestion recommendations and allow one-click application of suggested batching profiles to routes.

Non-functional Requirements:

- NFR-001: The runtime changes must not increase average per-token cost by > 2% across typical hosted workloads.
- NFR-002: Canary evaluation latency must be <= 30s for 5k requests sample window.
- NFR-003: Circuit breaker detection and automatic fallback must engage within 60s of crossing thresholds for 95% of incidents.
- NFR-004: All new telemetry must be captured and retained per existing observability retention SLAs (30 days standard, 90 days enterprise add-on).

Design Specifications (High-level):

Architecture overview:
- The runtime will include a Canary Manager service that subscribes to route configuration and coordinates gradual traffic shifts using the existing routing plane. Canary Manager tasks:
  - Orchestrate percentage-based traffic shifts.
  - Collect canary metrics (latency distribution, token counts, model quality signals) via a push pipeline to the evaluation store.
  - Trigger rollback or promote decisions based on policy evaluation.

- Circuit breakers will be implemented at the edge routing layer with a lightweight evaluation loop that monitors aggregated metrics from in-memory counters and enriches with streaming observed telemetry. When thresholds are crossed, the router marks route as degraded and routes to fallback model variant(s).

API Changes (examples):
- POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/canary
  Payload example:
  {
    "canary_percentage": 10,
    "model_variant": "unified/v27-beta",
    "metrics": {"p95_latency_ms": 200, "error_rate_pct": 1.0},
    "rollout_policy": "auto-promote-on-success"
  }

- PUT /v1/routes/{route_id}/circuit-breaker
  Payload example:
  {
    "latency_ms": 500,
    "error_rate_pct": 5.0,
    "token_cost_usd": 0.02,
    "fallback_model": "unified/v26-stable"
  }

Data model and storage:
- Canary evaluations stored in the evaluation store (time-series + sample traces). Each evaluation record includes route_id, canary_version, start_time, end_time, sample_size, and metrics_aggregates. Store schema is append-only and compatible with existing evaluation dashboards.

Operational runbooks (brief):
1) Launch Canary
  1. Create canary config via API or Console.
  2. Monitor Canary Manager dashboard for metrics and quality signals.
  3. If metrics cross thresholds, Canary Manager will auto-rollback; operations may also manually rollback via API.

2) Circuit Breaker Trigger
  1. Router marks route as degraded.
  2. Router switches traffic to fallback model(s) and emits an event to incident channels.
  3. On detection, follow rollback playbook and open incident if fallback persists > 5 minutes.

Roadmap & Themes (next 6 months):

- Q2 2026 (Current): Finish Canary Manager MVP, router circuit breaker core, Reserved Plus billing model implementation, and Console UX for recommendations.
- Q3 2026: Expand canary quality signals with model-eval integrations (automated evals tied to prompt sets), add rollout A/B test capabilities, and pilot Reserved Plus with ~10 mid-market customers.
- Q4 2026: GA release of canary rollouts, Reserved Plus general availability, deeper SSO & enterprise billing integrations, and additional observability retention tiers.

Prioritization rationale:
- Performance isolation and break/fallback features reduce operational risk and are high priority for enterprise renewals.
- Pricing simplification addresses friction in mid-market adoption.

Pricing & Packaging Notes (summary):

Objective: Introduce a mid-market-friendly commitment tier (Reserved Plus) that balances discount and flexibility while preserving upsell paths to Dedicated.

Reserved Plus details (proposal):
- Commitment: monthly commit (example: $12k/month) with a defined token allotment (e.g., 300M tokens) and 10% burst credits.
- Unit pricing: simplified blended rate for text tokens and embeddings (e.g., $0.0008 per text token equivalent, $0.0025 per embedding unit) after commitment is consumed.
- Console: customers can view committed vs. burst usage with projected overage estimates and opt-in auto-burn for burst credits.
- Billing: monthly invoice with true-up for overages at blended overage rate.

Migration & Sales guidance:
- Sales playbook: position Reserved Plus as lower-friction alternative to full Dedicated for customers who need predictable costs but not isolated capacity. Include TCO comparison tool in deck.
- Self-serve path: allow trial customers to convert to Reserved Plus in Console with identity verification and automated contract generation for standard terms.

Release Notes — v27 (June 2026):

Shipping features:
- Canary Manager MVP (API + Console) with percent-based canary rollouts and automatic promotion/rollback policies.
- Router circuit breakers with configurable thresholds (latency, error rate, token cost) and fallback routing to compatible model variants.
- Reserved Plus pricing tier added to billing system and Console (UI for commit selection and burst management).
- Console: cost suggestion panel surfaced on route pages and one-click batching profile application.

Known limitations (v27):
- Canary Manager currently evaluates only high-level metrics (latency, error rate); model-quality eval integrations are planned for Q3.
- Reserved Plus currently supports monthly commitments only; annual commitments will be added in Q4.
- Circuit breaker heuristic tuning requires production traffic to stabilize thresholds; default thresholds are conservative.

Launch & Rollout Plan:

- Internal Beta (2 weeks): rollout Canary Manager to internal teams and a 3-customer pilot for Reserved Plus.
- External Pilot (6 weeks): invite 8-12 mid-market customers and 3 enterprise early-adopters for Dedicated/Private rollout testing.
- Gradual GA (4 weeks): open Reserved Plus self-serve in Console to existing trial customers and new sign-ups in selected regions (US, EU).

Monitoring & KPIs Post-Launch:

- Telemetry to monitor: per-route P50/P95 latency, error rate, canary sample quality metrics, token counts, commit utilization %, and number of rollbacks.
- Dashboards: add a v27 release dashboard (template) to the Console and internal SRE dashboards.
- Alerting: create alerts for canary regression (promotable false negatives) and circuit breaker flapping.

Open Questions & Risks:

- Q1: How aggressive should default circuit breaker thresholds be to balance availability vs unnecessary fallbacks? (Action: product + SRE to define conservative defaults; operations to tune after pilot).
- Q2: Reserved Plus pricing sensitivity for churn—what discount vs flexibility yields best conversion? (Action: finance to simulate price points and run pilot offers).
- Risk: Early canary false positives due to noisy sampling could lead to unnecessary rollbacks; mitigation: increase sample size and combine quality signals before auto-rollback.

Appendix (examples & config table):

Canary policy fields (table represented in text):
- field: description: default
- canary_percentage: percentage of traffic routed to canary: 10
- sample_window_s: evaluation window in seconds: 300
- p95_latency_ms: maximum acceptable p95 latency for canary: 200
- error_rate_pct: maximum acceptable error rate: 1.0
- promotion_criteria: criteria for auto-promote: all_metrics_within_threshold

Example CLI to create a canary via the Redwood CLI:

redwood routes canary create --route-id chat-recommendations --percentage 10 --model unified/v27-beta --p95-latency 200 --error-rate 1.0 --auto-promote

API example (curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/chat-recommendations/canary -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"canary_percentage":10, "model_variant":"unified/v27-beta", "metrics":{"p95_latency_ms":200, "error_rate_pct":1.0}, "rollout_policy":"auto-promote-on-success" }'
